facts.statement: Crymocetus means "cold sea monster" and is an extinct reptile from the Late Cretaceous Chalk Group of Sussex, England.
facts.quote: Crymocetus (meaning "cold sea monster") is an extinct genus of Reptilia from the Late Cretaceous Chalk Group of Sussex, England.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Crymocetus is a single posterior cervical vertebra found in the Chalk Group of Sussex, England.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a single posterior cervical vertebra which was discovered in the Chalk Group in Sussex, England.

facts.statement: The species was first described as Plesiosaurus bernardi by Sir Richard Owen in 1850.
facts.quote: It was first named as Plesiosaurus bernardi by Owen (1850).

facts.statement: Edward Drinker Cope established the genus Crymocetus in 1869 after re-examining the holotype of Plesiosaurus bernardi.
facts.quote: However, Cope (1869) re-studied the holotype and decided that P. bernardi warranted its own genus, which he named Crymocetus.

facts.statement: Cope originally placed Crymocetus in Elasmosauridae, but later researchers suggested it belonged to Pliosauridae or Rhomaleosauridae.
facts.quote: Cope (1869) initially classified Crymocetus within Elasmosauridae, while Welles (1962) and Persson (1963) instead considered Crymocetus to be either a member of the Pliosauridae or Rhomaleosauridae.

facts.statement: Crymocetus is currently classified within Plesiosauria incertae sedis due to uncertain placement.
facts.quote: Crymocetus is today classified within Plesiosauria incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Many paleontologists ignored Cope's name Crymocetus, and Lydekker synonymized it with Cimoliasaurus in 1889.
facts.quote: After Cope (1869) was published, nearly all subsequent authors tended to disregard the name Crymocetus, with Lydekker (1889) synonymising Crymocetus with Cimoliasaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Crymocetus requires a restudy alongside other Cretaceous plesiosaurs from England.
facts.quote: In any case, Crymocetus is in need of restudy along with other plesiosaurs from the Cretaceous deposits of England.
